---
title: "Install"
subtitle: "Docker, the supported path, and a native install for those who manage their own environment"
---

## With Docker (recommended)

One image carries Python, R, the `falconage` command and every bundled clock at pinned versions,
so the same input gives the same numbers on any machine. Nothing else needs installing.

**1. Install Docker.** [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/) on
Windows or macOS, Docker Engine on Linux. Start it, then check it answers:

```bash
docker --version
```

"command not found" or "cannot connect to the Docker daemon" means Docker is not installed or not
running; nothing below works until it is.

**2. Get the image:**

```bash
docker pull bhagesh/falconage:1.0.0-cpu
```

**3. Check it:**

```bash
docker run --rm bhagesh/falconage:1.0.0-cpu config
```

::: {.falcon-output}
```
FALCONAge 1.0.0
  registry     1.1.0  (68 human clocks, 68 score offline)
  numpy        2.5.1
  cpu cores    8
```
:::

That is the whole install. [Your first run](quickstart.qmd) is the next step.

### Which image

| Tag | Contains | Use it when |
|---|---|---|
| `1.0.0-cpu` (also `latest`) | Python, R, the command line, every reader | Almost always |
| `1.0.0-py` | Python and the command line; no R, and no parquet or `.h5ad` reader | You only use Python or the command line, on CSV, TSV, GEO series, clinical or NMR files, and want a smaller download |

### Typing the commands

`"$PWD"` in the commands on this site means "the folder I am in now", and it is spelled
differently in each shell:

| Where you are typing | Write |
|---|---|
| macOS Terminal, Linux, Git Bash, WSL | `"$PWD"` |
| Windows PowerShell | `"${PWD}"` |
| Windows `cmd.exe` | `"%cd%"` |

A path error on Windows is almost always this.

The image's entrypoint is the `falconage` command, so the first word after the image name is a
verb: `demo`, `run`, `config`, `clocks`. The exceptions are `python`, `R`, `Rscript` and `bash`,
which open that program inside the image:

```bash
docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/work" bhagesh/falconage:1.0.0-cpu python
docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/work" bhagesh/falconage:1.0.0-cpu R
```

On Linux, if the run cannot write into your folder ("Permission denied"), run the container as
yourself by adding `-u "$(id -u):$(id -g)"` after `docker run --rm`.

### Keeping downloads between runs

Nothing bundled needs the network. Public data fetched with `falconage download` is cached. Add a
named volume so a new container does not fetch it again:

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" -v falconage-cache:/opt/falconage/cache \
  bhagesh/falconage:1.0.0-cpu download GSE40279
```

### Building the image yourself

Both images are published, so pulling is the two-minute route:

```bash
docker pull bhagesh/falconage:1.0.0-cpu
docker pull bhagesh/falconage:1.0.0-py
```

To build them from a clone of the repository instead, about ten minutes the first time:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bhagesh-h/FALCONAge.git
cd FALCONAge
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile.cpu -t bhagesh/falconage:1.0.0-cpu .
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile.cpu --target py -t bhagesh/falconage:1.0.0-py .
```

## Without Docker

If you already manage your own Python or R environment.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Python

```bash
pip install "falconage[plot] @ git+https://github.com/bhagesh-h/FALCONAge.git#subdirectory=python"
falconage config
```

Optional extras: `methylation` (parquet), `anndata` (`.h5ad`), `metabolomics` (Nightingale
`.xlsx`), or `all`.

### R

```r
remotes::install_github("bhagesh-h/FALCONAge", subdir = "r")

library(FALCONAge)
falconage_install()   # builds the Python environment R calls into; a few minutes
falconage_config()    # what resolved: versions, registry size
```

The R package hands every number to the Python core, so it needs a Python environment either
way. On reticulate 1.41 or later one is built on first use and `falconage_install()` is optional;
use it when you want a pinned, reproducible environment.

:::

Every command on this site works the same in a native install; only the
`docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" bhagesh/falconage:1.0.0-cpu` prefix goes away.

## When something looks wrong

Run `falconage config` (or `falconage_config()` in R) first. It reports the version, the registry
and how many clocks are usable, and it is the first thing to include in a bug report.
